claim.pdf_says: 14.9.30.4   General rules   (a fourth-level clause subordinate to 14.9.30 READ statement, printed in the same style as 14.9.30.1 General and 14.9.30.2 General formats)
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.30.4 General rules   (H2 - the same level as the parent '## 14.9.30 READ statement', while siblings .1 and .2 are '###')
claim.why_it_matters: Same structural defect as 14.9.30.3: the General rules clause is promoted out of READ, so the outline no longer shows it as part of the READ statement. Neighbouring statements are transcribed correctly ('### 14.9.29.4 General rules', '### 14.9.31.4 General rules').

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and every factual assertion in the claim holds.

PDF (rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v724/spec_p724.png, printed page 694): the page opens with the bold heading '14.9.30.4   General rules', followed by 'ALL FORMATS' and general rules 1)-8) of the READ statement. Comparison page 722 (printed 692) shows '14.9.30   READ statement', '14.9.30.1   General' and '14.9.30.2   General formats' in the identical bold face and size - the PDF supplies NO font cue distinguishing the levels, so the clause hierarchy is carried solely by the dotted clause number. By that numbering, 14.9.30.4 is unambiguously subordinate to 14.9.30.

Markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md): line 29545 is '## 14.9.30.4 General rules' (H2). Its parent at line 29441 is '## 14.9.30 READ statement' (also H2), so the two are encoded as peers. Its own siblings are H3 - line 29444 '### 14.9.30.1 General', line 29449 '### 14.9.30.2 General formats' - and the analogous clauses of the immediately adjacent statements are H3 as well: line 29421 '### 14.9.29.4 General rules', line 29838 '### 14.9.31.4 General rules'. The claim quotes both sources accurately.

Adversarial checks, all of which failed to refute:
- Text present elsewhere / reflowed? No. The heading text is present and verbatim correct; the defect is depth, not presence, so 'missing' does not apply but the discrepancy is not thereby dissolved.
- Merely formatting? No. In a Markdown transcription of a numbered standard the heading level IS the encoding of the clause hierarchy - it drives TOC generation, section slicing and anchor nesting. Any consumer that reads outline depth places 'General rules' as a sibling of 'READ statement' rather than inside it, which misrepresents the PDF's structure. This is a different class from line wrapping, hyphenation or page-break furniture.
- An alternative but self-consistent convention? No. The file's own convention is overwhelmingly component-count -> heading depth: 620 of 782 four-component headings are H3. The H2 here is an error by the transcription's own standard.

The normative content is not damaged: the clause number '14.9.30.4' is transcribed correctly, so citation-by-number still resolves, the rule text 1)-8) is complete and in the right reading order, and no semantics change. Severity is correctly 'structural', not 'content'.
verdict.corrected_description:
Real, but mislabelled and mis-scoped by the claim.

(1) Wrong kind. Nothing is missing. The heading '14.9.30.4 General rules' is transcribed verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29545. The defect is HEADING PROMOTION / wrong outline depth: it is emitted as '##' (H2) instead of '###' (H3), making it a markdown-level peer of its own parent '## 14.9.30 READ statement' (line 29441). Kind should be 'heading-level' or 'heading-promotion', not 'missing-heading'.

(2) Wrong scope. 'Neighbouring statements are transcribed correctly' is true locally but wrongly implies an isolated slip. Document-wide, 162 of 782 four-component headings (21%) carry the same H2 promotion, and the artifact is heavily concentrated at page boundaries: 45 of the 52 four-component headings that sit at the top of a page marker are H2 (86%), versus 117 of 730 mid-page (16%). Page 724's instance is one of that cohort - 14.9.30.4 is the first heading on the page, exactly like 14.9.30.3 at the top of page 723 (line 29499). The transcription pipeline appears to lose enclosing-hierarchy context when it starts a new page, and sporadically elsewhere.

(3) Correct remediation. Fix by a global sweep that derives heading depth from the dotted clause number's component count (3 components -> H2, 4 -> H3, and so on), re-leveling all 162 offenders, rather than by a one-off edit to line 29545. The PDF provides no font cue to distinguish these levels - on page 722 '14.9.30', '14.9.30.1' and '14.9.30.2' are set in identical bold - so the numbering is the only authority for depth and is the correct basis for the sweep.

(4) Impact, stated precisely. No normative content is lost or altered; rules 1)-8) are complete and correct, and citation by clause number is unaffected. The harm is confined to outline/TOC nesting and any tooling that slices sections by markdown heading depth.
